title: Rabbi Yitzchak bar Bar Chana
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: [Yoma 77b](https://www.sefaria.org/Yoma.77b.8) quotes him saying, “I saw Zeiri go to visit his student Rav Chiya bar Ashi.” Dikdukei Soferim reads Rabbi Yitzchak bar Rav Chana. In [Bava Kamma 52a](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Kamma.52a.11) he explains that it became wormy within. Hyman says Seder HaDorot conflated this Amora with Rav Yitzchak, son of Rabbah bar bar Chana, whereas they were two sages who lived at different times.[^1]

notes.text: Yoma gives Rav Yitzchak and the two opposite directions of the visit. Bava Kamma gives Rabbi Yitzchak in the case of a pit cover that became worm-eaten. [Heilprin](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=2206&lang=en) assigns both passages to Rabbah bar bar Chana’s son. Hyman insists on two men of different periods; the reported Dikdukei Soferim form remains his attribution.
